transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

I came in because I keep hearing Garrett’s voice. It’s not like a memory or a thought — it sounds clear, like he’s right behind me, sometimes when I’m on the trail or in my painting room. I know, at least part of me knows, that he’s dead, but when it happens it feels completely real.
Who is Garrett to you?
Garrett was… someone important to me. I’m sorry, I don’t really know how to explain it more than that right now.
Did Garrett die recently?
Yes. It’s been about a month since Garrett died, and… this whole thing has been unfolding since then.
Aside from hearing Garrett’s voice, have you had any other experiences that felt unreal or strange, like seeing things that others couldn’t see?

Not really seeing things, no. It’s mainly Garrett’s voice. I’ll be on the trail or in my painting room, and it’s so clear it feels like he’s standing right behind me. I know he’s dead, but when it happens, it feels real.
Since Garrett died, have you been feeling depressed most of the day nearly every day?
I don’t really know if I’d call it depressed most of the day, nearly every day. I’ve been upset and not myself since he died, but I haven’t been tracking it that clearly.
Do you believe Garrett is actually speaking to you from the outside world?

Part of me knows Garrett is dead, so I can’t really say that makes sense. But when I hear his voice, it’s so clear—like he’s right behind me on the trail or in my painting room—that in that moment it feels like he’s actually there speaking to me.
Right now, do you believe Garrett is truly speaking to you?

Right now… I know Garrett is dead, so part of me knows it shouldn’t be possible. But when I hear him, it’s so clear—like he’s standing right behind me—that in that moment it feels completely real, like he’s actually speaking to me.
Since Garrett died, have you been feeling down or depressed most days?
I’m not sure. I’ve had some bad stretches since he died, and I’ve felt off, but I don’t know if I’d say it’s been most days.
Do you believe Garrett is still alive?
I don’t think he’s alive, no. I know he died. It’s just… sometimes what I experience makes that feel less clear in the moment.
Have you had any strongly held beliefs lately that other people would say aren’t true?

I don’t think so. I mean, not that I can point to. I’ve had experiences that feel very real in the moment, but I’m not walking around convinced of some specific thing that other people are telling me is false.
Have you noticed your thoughts getting jumbled or hard to organize lately?

Yeah. They don’t feel exactly jumbled, but they move too fast. I’ll start thinking about one patient note, and then suddenly it’s five different work projects, then some random memory from a hike, then feeling guilty about the funeral, all before I can really catch up to any of it.
Since Garrett died, have you had times when you felt unusually energized or high?

Yeah. Especially at first after he died, I felt almost… lit up. Like I had some urgent purpose, like I could see what needed to happen and nobody else could. But if anyone questioned me or tried to slow me down, I’d get furious really fast.
During that energized period after Garrett died, did you need much less sleep than usual?

Yes. For weeks I was only sleeping maybe two or three hours a night, but I didn’t feel tired. I felt wired, like I could just keep going. Then later I started crashing, but it wasn’t restful—more like broken, heavy sleep, and I’d still wake up before dawn exhausted and panicky.
During that energized period, did you believe you had special abilities or a special mission that other people didn’t understand?

I don’t know that I’d put it that way. I definitely felt like I understood something other people weren’t seeing, like I had to push things forward. But “special abilities” or a “mission” feels… I’m not sure. It felt important at the time, but I don’t know how to describe it beyond that.
Did you hear Garrett’s voice during the time when you were sleeping only two or three hours a night?

Yes. That was when it started. When I was barely sleeping and felt wired, like I had to keep pushing and taking on things I couldn’t really handle, that’s when I first heard Garrett’s voice. I hadn’t heard him like that before, and it didn’t feel like just normal grief.
Have you ever heard Garrett’s voice at a time when you were not feeling unusually energized or wired?

No, not really. It started during that wired stretch when I was barely sleeping and taking on things I couldn’t realistically do, but felt like I had to keep going. Before that shift, I hadn’t heard Garrett’s voice like that, not even in just ordinary grief.
